title: Pushout of an extension gives the contracted-product torsor
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $G,G'$ abelian sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ [def-sc-zariski-site, def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], and $\varphi:G\to G'$ a morphism. Let $0\to G\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{p}\mathbf Z_X\to0$ be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves, where $\mathbf Z_X$ is the constant integer sheaf. Its *fibre over $1$* is $T=E\times_{\mathbf Z_X,1}*$, the sheaf of lifts of the global section $1$, with $G$ acting by translation through $j$. Define the *pushout extension* $E_{\varphi}=(E\oplus G')/\{(j(g),-\varphi(g)):g\in G\}$, with its induced injection of $G'$ and projection to $\mathbf Z_X$. Define the *contracted product* $T\wedge^G G'$ as the sheafification of $(T\times G')/G$ for $g\cdot(t,g')=(g\cdot t,\varphi(g)^{-1}g')$. Then $0\to G'\to E_{\varphi}\to\mathbf Z_X\to0$ is short exact and its fibre over $1$ is canonically the $G'$-torsor $T\wedge^G G'$ [def-sc-gm-torsor].

source.place: Lemma 02FQ, proof via the boundary of 1 and functoriality under a morphism of coefficient sheaves

proof.text: In the abelian category of abelian sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], the quotient of $E\oplus G'$ by the image of $g\mapsto(j(g),-\varphi(g))$ has the universal property of the pushout of $j:G\to E$ along $\varphi:G\to G'$: a pair of morphisms from $E$ and $G'$ agrees on $G$ exactly when the induced map from $E\oplus G'$ kills that image. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pushout-short-exact-sequence] to the given short exact sequence and this pushout. It supplies the induced projection $E_{\varphi}\to\mathbf Z_X$ and proves that $0\to G'\to E_{\varphi}\to\mathbf Z_X\to0$ is short exact.

source.place: Lemma 02FQ, pushout extension in the proof of the torsor--H^1 correspondence

proof.text: A local section of the fibre of $E_{\varphi}\to\mathbf Z_X$ over $1$ is represented by a pair $(t,g')$ with $t\in T$ and $g'\in G'$, since the first component must map to $1$. Locally means: $E\oplus G'\to E_{\varphi}$ is an epimorphism, so by [lem-sc-abelian-sheaf-short-exact-stalkwise] it is surjective on stalks, and every germ of $E_{\varphi}$ comes from a germ of $E\oplus G'$. Two such pairs represent the same section precisely when they differ by $(j(g),-\varphi(g))$ for a local section $g$ of $G$, which is the relation $(t,g')\sim(g\cdot t,\varphi(g)^{-1}g')$. Thus the fibre is canonically the sheafification of $(T\times G')/G$, namely $T\wedge^G G'$, and the induced $G'$-translation agrees with the second-factor action.

source.place: Lemma 02FQ, identification of the fibre over 1 of the pushout extension

proof.text: The fibre over $1$ of a short exact sequence $0\to G'\to E_{\varphi}\to\mathbf Z_X\to0$ is a $G'$-torsor: lifts of $1$ exist locally, since by [lem-sc-abelian-sheaf-short-exact-stalkwise] the stalk maps of $E_{\varphi}\to\mathbf Z_X$ are surjective, so the germ of $1$ at each point lifts to a germ, represented on a neighbourhood where it maps to $1$, and any two lifts differ by a unique section of the kernel $G'$. Therefore the canonical identification in Step 2 is an identification of $G'$-torsors.

lean.statement: theorem zariski_torsor_extension_pushout (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{uE}) {G G' E : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{uE}} (φ : G ⟶ G') (j : G ⟶ E) (p : E ⟶ (constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{uE}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{uE} ℤ))) (hjp : j ≫ p = 0) (hE : (ShortComplex.mk j p hjp).ShortExact) : ∃ (p' : pushout j φ ⟶ (constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{uE}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{uE} ℤ))), pushout.inl j φ ≫ p' = p ∧ ∃ (hz : pushout.inr j φ ≫ p' = 0), (ShortComplex.mk (pushout.inr j φ) p' hz).ShortExact ∧ ∃ (T : Torsor G) (T' : Torsor G') (a : ∀ U : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ, T.sheaf.obj.obj U → E.obj.obj U) (b : ∀ U : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ, T'.sheaf.obj.obj U → (pushout j φ).obj.obj U) (q : ZariskiContractedProductPresentation X φ T T'), (∀ ⦃U V : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ⦄ (f : U ⟶ V) (t : T.sheaf.obj.obj U), E.obj.map f (a U t) = a V (T.sheaf.obj.map f t)) ∧ (∀ U : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ, Set.BijOn (a U) Set.univ {e | p.hom.app U e = (toSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) ((Functor.const (Opens X)ᵒᵖ).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{uE} ℤ)))).app U ⟨1⟩}) ∧ (∀ (U : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ) (g : G.obj.obj U) (t : T.sheaf.obj.obj U), a U (T.vadd U g t) = a U t + j.hom.app U g) ∧ (∀ ⦃U V : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ⦄ (f : U ⟶ V) (t : T'.sheaf.obj.obj U), (pushout j φ).obj.map f (b U t) = b V (T'.sheaf.obj.map f t)) ∧ (∀ U : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ, Set.BijOn (b U) Set.univ {e | p'.hom.app U e = (toSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) ((Functor.const (Opens X)ᵒᵖ).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{uE} ℤ)))).app U ⟨1⟩}) ∧ (∀ (U : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ) (h : G'.obj.obj U) (t : T'.sheaf.obj.obj U), b U (T'.vadd U h t) = b U t + (pushout.inr j φ).hom.app U h) ∧ (∀ (U : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ) (t : T.sheaf.obj.obj U) (h : G'.obj.obj U), b U (q.quotient U t h) = (pushout.inl j φ).hom.app U (a U t) + (pushout.inr j φ).hom.app U h)
